I was about to spin up a few vms to test a node based server structure. I started thinking what documentation do I need to look at to make sure I get them networked well. Then the thought hit me, multiple loopback.

It's very simple 

ifconfig lo:0 127.0.0.2 netmask 255.0.0.1 up
ifconfig lo:1 127.0.0.3 netmask 255.0.0.1 up
ifconfig lo:2 127.0.0.4 netmask 255.0.0.1 up
ifconfig lo:3 127.0.0.5 netmask 255.0.0.1 up

Now edit your /etc/hosts

127.0.0.2 cdnroot
127.0.0.3 cdn1.cdnroot
127.0.0.4 cdn2.cdnroot
127.0.0.5 cdn3.cdnroot

Now you can bind multiple servers on port 80 without interference and chances are whatever server software you're using it can likely just use the domains defined in the hosts file rather than remembering ips for the bind.

Why do with vms what can be done with relatively basic sysadmin skills... (I'm looking at you docker).
Setting up multiple loopback for testing multiple servers on one box

You could simply build a bridge, which would allow those guests internet access and internal access.

Depending on distro, look up

Brctl

The issue is it eats up ram just to test a few servers and it's more difficult to switch between them and do initial setup. People are under utilizing what a single machine can do.

The initial plan was to use a bridge, but then this was easier.
